top_choice_rationale: P003 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) ranks first because its central findings are the most thoroughly confronted with data. The skill-premium results have been reproduced across countries and periods, and the China-shock designs have been re-analysed and criticised for about a decade. The qualitative conclusion that adjustment costs are concentrated and persistent in exposed local labour markets has survived, although magnitudes are still debated. The citation can credit this empirical and conceptual body of work without claiming a precise effect size. I accept the weaknesses. The task and trade-shock strands may be two achievements, Dorn is omitted, part of the task theory belongs to Acemoglu and Restrepo, and the 2023-24 prizes are thematically close. P001 is my second choice because its two-author attribution is cleanest and the mechanism is mature, though the collateral channel is identified only indirectly and the citation must credit the mechanism, not a magnitude. P002 follows closely because of its direct firm-level testing, but its attribution is harder to draw (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and the Krugman 2008 overlap). All three proposals are preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. No listed co-author or institutional tie to Autor, Hanson, Katz, Kiyotaki, Moore, Helpman or Melitz. My metascience and replication interests may bias me toward work with a strong re-analysis record, and I note this as a possible bias.
